title: R' Yosi son of R' Shalom
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: R' Yosi son of R' Shalom.

He is mentioned in the old Midrash Tehillim, at the beginning of chapter 72. The annotator הרש״ב already observed there that the reading should be R' Yehudah son of R' Shalom. In Seder HaDorot, the printers confused matters and wrote: ‘R' Yosi ben Shalom said: My father had goats,’ etc. They did not see that the saying ‘My father had goats’ belongs to the preceding entry, Rabbi Yosi ben Dolgai. Here it should read R' Yosi son of R' Shalom, from Shocher Tov. This is clear. Maskil LeEitan did not notice this.[^1]

notes.text: The earlier proofread text gives עוים היו לאבא twice. The saying is rendered here by the source-supported reading עזים היו לאבא, ‘My father had goats’: the named William Davidson Hebrew edition of [Yoma 39b:13](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.39b.13) gives this phrase in Rabbi (Yosi ben) Dolgai’s saying. The complete native notice on PDF page 319 was also inspected. This corrects the English reading without changing the canonical Hebrew. It does not independently verify Hyman’s account of the printers of Seder HaDorot. The heading’s בר׳ means son of R', preserving the abbreviated title, distinct from the printers’ בן שלום without that title. סה״ד is Seder HaDorot; שה״ט is the contextual title Shocher Tov, and משה״ט means ‘from Shocher Tov.’ The exact locator שה״ט סע״ב remains unconverted; רפ״עב means the beginning of chapter 72. הרש״ב remains unexpanded. ‘This is clear’ retains Hyman’s confidence, not an independent adjudication of his textual history.

The full Rabbi title for Yosi ben Dolgai is supplied by the checked Yoma passage. The retrieved digital Midrash Tehillim 72 begins with the abbreviated אר״י בר שלום; it does not establish a full personal title for Hyman’s Yosi or Yehudah son of Shalom. Those titles therefore remain R'. This title check does not resolve the annotator’s name, the Seder HaDorot printing history, or Hyman’s competing readings.
